title: Low Energy Ion Thinning of Frozen Biological Specimens for Electron Cryomicroscopy
content: One possible strategy to solving a structure by electron cryomicroscopy is to thin a specimen frozen in thicker layer of amorphous ice, tissue or cell. However, the current approaches using a focused ion beam (FIB) [1] leave a damaged layer on the thinned surface, the depth of which depends on the energy of the ions used to bombard the surface. This damage layer has been observed and measured in specimens prepared by gallium or plasma source FIB [2,3].
